argument: The retained mistake must be actual bypass geometry: a line approaches a closed point, shifts into a side lane, travels alongside it, and returns downstream. Roof edge, ground, and route need to share that order from different origins.

Hide labels, readout, bridge, and bypass dots. A caption-free viewer should find repeated sideways departures, longer parallel runs, and later returns in all three drawing systems. If it reads as a decorative offset, the mutation fails.

Pointer, Enter, and Space must create a bounded bypass that changes the actual route field; lifting only the latest one must reproduce the exact prior geometry, including its side lane and downstream return.

A bypass is an easy metaphor. Delete v010 if the line never gets beside anything, if the return happens at the same point, if edge clicks produce no structural change, or if the prose explains more detour than the drawing can show.
